title: Smoothing a proper curve with isolated complete-intersection singularities
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $X$ be a proper $k$-scheme [def-weil-proper-morphism] of dimension at most one. Suppose $X$ is a local complete intersection over $k$: it has an affine open cover by spectra of finitely generated $k$-algebras that are local complete intersections in [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. Suppose $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] away from finitely many closed points. There exists a flat finitely presented projective morphism $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k[[t]]$ whose special fibre is $k$-isomorphic to $X$ and whose generic fibre over $k((t))$ is smooth. Projective is in the finite-projective-space convention [def-kun-projective]; $k[[t]]$ is the formal power-series ring and $k((t))=k[[t]][1/t]$.

source.place: Tag 0E7Y, lemma-smoothing-proper-curve-isolated-lci. Finite presentation follows because the base k[[t]] and its finite projective spaces are Noetherian.

proof.text: Apply the lci pointwise criterion at each x. Its regular presentation has quotient by the span of the range of the list entries; identify that ideal with Ideal.ofList. The regular sequence generates a proper ideal, hence its entries lie in the maximal ideal. The quotient is essentially finite type by surjectivity. These data give the existing complete-intersection-local-algebra predicate.

Enumerate the finite set of closed points by Fin r and retain injectivity, closedness, and smoothness away from its range. At each marked stalk apply the local Fitting smoothing theorem to the complete-intersection local algebra from the preceding step. Choose its B_i, special-fibre algebra isomorphism, finite generating surjection and parameter-power bound. All choices occur inside the proof of the existential theorem.

Apply the prescribed-local-deformation algebraization lemma to these B_i. This constructs the proper flat finitely presented H-projective family Y, its special-fibre isomorphism, and scalar-compatible finite-jet stalk identifications. No lci or Fitting data are needed for this algebraization step.

Apply the local Fitting criterion to this already constructed family, its finite-jet identifications and the local bounds. It supplies a covering U_0,U_1 whose restricted maps are proper, whose special fibres are CM and pure of dimensions zero and one, and whose finite jets satisfy the required global Fitting memberships.

For each U_d apply the finite-jet smooth-generic-fibre theorem. The canonical R-algebra equivalence between the localization R[1/t] and LaurentSeries k induces a base isomorphism; its pullback transports smoothness to the specified localization. Pull back the covering U_0,U_1 to the generic fibre. Pasting pullback squares identifies its members with these smooth generic fibres. Source locality of smoothness gives smoothness of the entire generic fibre. Pair this with the flatness, finite-presentation, projectivity and special-fibre data already constructed.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0E7Y; algebraize the whole curve first, then partition the given proper flat family into dimension-zero and dimension-one pieces for the local Fitting calculation. The local/formal/Fitting route is unchanged; the disjoint-union embedding is unnecessary.
